Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- Buttons highlight again in games packaged by kagex-release with images converted to TLG or JPEG (the default): the framework only looked for a button's hover, pressed and focus images as PNG, TLG5, TLG6 or BMP. kagex-release now refuses those conversions for a game whose `data/system` predates this fix
- Web builds pick up updates: players kept getting the old game, because the engine caches every game file in the browser for good. Each build now has an id the page checks before the game starts, so a new upload reaches players on their next visit
- Web builds offer Add to Home Screen on phones and tablets, where the game then opens full screen: an Add button where the browser can install it (Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet, Opera), the steps on iPhone, iPad and in Firefox
- Web builds show a link preview in Discord, Slack, X and the like: the title, a description and a preview image. kagex-release has *Site address*, *Description* and *Preview image* settings for them
- kagex-release 0.3.1 downloads the 0.3.1 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.3.1/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
